court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: Inspector General of Registration and Others … Respondent(s).
advocates: For Petitioner(s): Ms. R. Amurtha for Mr. G. Ilamurugu
For Respondent(s): Mr. U. Baranidharan, Special Government Pleader for R 1 to R 3
prayer: PRAYER: Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, pleased to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the 2nd respondent to consider the petitioners complaint dated 07/08/2025 and there by directing the 2nd respondent to take action under section 83 of the Registration Act, 1908.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, J.:— Asserting that the petitioner's paternal grandfather purchased an extent of 2.46 acres in Survey No. 370/4 Ayanperayur Village under Sale deed dated 10.02.1975 bearing Document No. 305 of 1975, the petitioner has approached this Court by submitting representations seeking action under Section 83 of the Registration Act, 1908.

2. Mr. U. Baranidharan, learned Special Government Pleader, accepts notice for respondents 1 to 3. Referring to the petition dated 20.08.2025 under Section 83 of the Registration Act, he points out that the petitioner is complaining about Document No. 913 of 2011, Document No. 3 of 2018, Document No. 5245 of 2024 and the like. He points out that the registering officer does not have the power of cancellation.

3. As submitted by learned Special Government Pleader, the registering officer does not have the power of cancellation. Besides, the petitioner has submitted representations in August 2025 in respect of registrations made from the year 2011. No acceptable explanation for the inordinate delay is contained in the affidavit in support of the writ petition. In these circumstances, no useful purpose would be served in directing consideration of the petitioner's representation. Leaving it open to the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional civil court, this writ petition is disposed of. No costs.
